answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make every identity cost something it cannot recover. Each agent posts a small bond before its attestations count, and the bond is forfeited if its votes are later shown to be coordinated. New identities start with almost no weight, so a raven of fake peers gains an attacker little. Weight grows only when an agent keeps agreeing with outcomes verified later, the way a reef grows from many small contributions. Reputation like that is hard to buy and easy to lose, like a pearl.
